title: ～っけ — was it ～? (recalling)
summary: A casual sentence-ending used when trying to recall something half-forgotten or checking a memory. It follows the plain form (だ with nouns and な-adjectives).

patterns.form: 普通形（名詞・Aな＋だ）＋っけ

body.p: 何時からだっけ and 何だっけ show you should know the answer but have forgotten and are trying to recall it. It can be a murmur or a question to someone. ～たっけ asks about a past memory.
Casual talk with friends and family. With superiors switch to a polite form like ～でしたか. ～だったっけ is for checking a past fact.

examples.ja: 明日（あした）の会議（かいぎ）は何時（なんじ）からだっけ。
examples.romaji: Ashita no kaigi wa nanji kara dakke.
examples.tr: What time was tomorrow's meeting again?

examples.ja: あれ、この漢字（かんじ）の読（よ）み方（かた）は何（なん）だっけ。
examples.romaji: Are, kono kanji no yomikata wa nan dakke.
examples.tr: Huh, what was the reading of this kanji again?

examples.ja: 君（きみ）の誕生日（たんじょうび）は来週（らいしゅう）だったっけ。
examples.romaji: Kimi no tanjōbi wa raishū datta kke.
examples.tr: Your birthday was next week, right?

pitfalls: It can refer to future plans, but only when you have forgotten or are unsure. It is not for things you are learning for the first time.
It is casual, so avoid it with superiors and in writing.
